claim: Cops3 subunit of the CSN interacts with the cytoplasmic tail of Dsg1 in yeast two-hybrid assays.
source: Cops3 could interact with the constructs comprising the full cytoplasmic tail of Dsg1 or a construct lacking only the membrane proximal intracellular anchor (IA) in yeast (Figure 1a).
evidence: Demonstrated through yeast two-hybrid growth assays shown in Figure 1a

claim: The interaction between Cops3 and Dsg1 is selective, as Cops4 does not interact with the Dsg1 tail.
source: The interaction with Cops3 was selective, as the fourth subunit of the CSN was unable to interact with the Dsg1 tail in yeast (Figure 1b).
evidence: Negative control experiment shown in Figure 1b demonstrating specificity

claim: Recombinant GST-Dsg1 binds to endogenous Cops3 from NHEK lysates in vitro.
source: Indeed, purified GST-Dsg1 bound to sepharose beads specifically precipitated endogenous Cops3 from NHEK lysates (Figure 1c).
evidence: GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 1c

claim: Endogenous Dp interacts with Cops3 in NHEKs after 1 day of differentiation.
source: Cops3 was also present in immunoprecipitates of endogenous Dp (Figure 1d).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1d

claim: The C-terminal tail of Dp is sufficient for interaction with Cops3.
source: While the N-terminal portion of Dp harboring the amino acid residues 1–584 (DP-NTP) was not sufficient for Dp's interaction with Cops3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), a 32 kDa truncated version of the C-terminal tail of Dp co-precipitated with endogenous Cops3 in the SCC9 cell line, which was used to overcome the limitations of ectopic expression of the Dp S-tag fusion protein (DP-S-tag) in primary cells. This suggested the site of interaction on Dp resides within the C-terminus (Figure 1e).
evidence: Domain mapping experiments using truncation constructs shown in Figure 1e and Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: Cops3 is distributed throughout the cell and closely associates with Dsg1 and Dp at cell-cell junctions and cytoplasmic particles.
source: SIM images revealed Cops3 to be distributed throughout the cell, impinging upon Dsg1 or Dp concentrated at cell-cell junctions. Cops3 was also closely associated with cytoplasmic Dsg1 and Dp particles, which could represent vesicles or cytoplasmic precursors, previously described (Godsel et al., 2005) (Figure 1f).
evidence: Structured illumination microscopy images shown in Figure 1f

claim: Dsg1 and Cops3 are in close proximity (40-100 nm) in NHEKs, as demonstrated by proximity ligation assay.
source: A positive PLA signal was observed for the Dsg1 and Cops3 antibody pair, which was abrogated by treatment with either DSG1 or COPS3 siRNA (Figure 1g and Figure 1—figure supplement 2), consistent with an association between Dsg1 and Cops3 in NHEKs.
evidence: Proximity ligation assay data shown in Figure 1g and Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: Dp and Cops3 are in close proximity in NHEKs treated with high calcium media to induce differentiation.
source: In addition, PLA analysis revealed a positive signal for Dp and Cops3 in NHEKs treated with high calcium media to induce epidermal differentiation, which was likewise inhibited through knockdown of Dp and Cops3 (Figure 1h and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Proximity ligation assay data shown in Figure 1h and Figure 1—figure supplement 3

claim: The integrity of the entire desmosome is required to scaffold the COP9 signalosome.
source: To investigate further the possibility that the entire desmosome serves as a docking site for the recruitment of the CSN, we also assessed whether Dp knockdown diminished Cops3's ability to co-localize with Dsg1 (Figure 1g) and vice versa (Figure 1h). In both cases, PLA signals were significantly reduced, supporting the idea that the integrity of the entire desmosome is required to scaffold the COP9 signalosome.
evidence: PLA experiments with reciprocal knockdowns shown in Figure 1g and 1h

claim: Cops3 interacts with desmosomal molecules Dsg1 and Dp but not with adherens junction components E-cadherin and Beta-catenin.
source: To address the specificity of Cops3 interactions with desmosomes we paired the Cops3 antibody with the adherens junction protein E-cadherin (E-cad). As a positive control, E-cad and Beta-catenin (B-cat) were paired as well as Alpha-catenin (A-cat) and B-cat (Figure 1i and Figure 1—figure supplement 4). These experiments clearly show that while Cops3 interacts with desmosomal molecules Dsg1 and Dp, it does not interact with adherens junction components.
evidence: PLA specificity controls shown in Figure 1i and Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: Approximately 60% of Dsg1/Cops3 PLA signals and 67% of Dp/Cops3 PLA signals are localized at cell-cell interfaces marked by Plakoglobin.
source: These data show that while not all desmosome-Cops3 interactions are in close proximity to the Pg signal, a large percentage of PLA dots do appear to be localized at cell-cell interfaces (~60% for Dsg1/Cops3;~67% for Dp/Cops3), although to a somewhat lesser extent than the positive control PLA pairings Alpha-Catenin/Beta-Catenin (~82%) and Ecad/Beta-catenin (~88%) (Figure 1i and Figure 1—figure supplement 4c).
evidence: Quantification of PLA signal localization shown in Figure 1i and Figure 1—figure supplement 4c

claim: Silencing COPS3 in NHEKs results in a reduction in differentiation markers including Dsg1, Dsc1, K1, and K10.
source: Biochemical analysis revealed a reduction in differentiation related gene products including Dsg1, Desmocollin1 (Dsc1), Keratin1 (K1), and Keratin 10 (K10) (Figure 2a).
evidence: Western blot analysis shown in Figure 2a

claim: Five independent siRNA oligos targeting COPS3 produce similar impairment of keratinocyte differentiation markers, supporting that observed changes are not due to off-target effects.
source: Similar impairment of these features of the keratinocyte differentiation program were observed using five oligos each with independent targets within the COPS3 sequence (siCOPS3-465, siCOPS3-Dharma3, siCOPS3-IDT pool including 3 oligos), supporting the idea that the observed changes were not due to off target effects (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Multiple independent siRNA sequences tested as shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Cops3-deficient 3D organotypic raft cultures show decreased expression of differentiation markers Dsg1, Dsc1, K1, K10, and Loricrin.
source: Biochemical analysis of raft lysates revealed similar differentiation defects when compared with monolayer cultures reflected by a decrease in Dsg1, Dsc1, the suprabasal keratins K1 and K10 and the cell envelope protein Loricrin (Lor) (Figure 2c).
evidence: Western blot analysis of 3D raft cultures shown in Figure 2c

claim: Immunofluorescence of siCOPS3 Day 3 rafts reveals defects in the differentiation markers K10 and Dsg1.
source: Immunofluorescence of siCOPS3 Day 3 rafts also revealed defects in the differentiation marker K10 and Dsg1 (Figure 2d).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2d

claim: Ectopic Dsg1-FLAG is unable to fully drive expression of differentiation markers Dsc1, K1, and K10 in Cops3-silenced cultures.
source: Biochemical analysis of cells retrovirally transduced with a Dsg1-Flag vector revealed that Dsg1-Flag was unable to drive expression of Dsc1, K1, and K10 in Cops3-silenced cultures after inducing differentiation for 2 days to the same extent as control cells (Figure 2e).
evidence: Western blot analysis of rescue experiment shown in Figure 2e

claim: Dsg1-GFP expressing cells are unable to express K10 upon silencing of COPS3 after 1 day of differentiation.
source: We observed that Dsg1-GFP expressing cells were unable to express K10 upon silencing of COPS3 (Figure 2f and g).
evidence: Immunofluorescence and quantification shown in Figure 2f and g

claim: Dsg1 requires Cops3 for efficient Dsg1-stimulated keratinocyte differentiation.
source: Thus, Dsg1 requires Cops3 for efficient Dsg1-stimulated keratinocyte differentiation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experiments showing Dsg1 cannot promote differentiation without Cops3

claim: Silencing COPS3 in NHEKs results in increases in pEGFR, pErk, and pMek.
source: Increases in pEGFR, phosphorylated Erk (pErk), and phosphorylated Mitogen Activated Protein Kinase (pMek) were observed (Figure 3a).
evidence: Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3a

claim: An increase in pErk is observed in 3D organotypic raft cultures treated with siRNA targeting COPS3.
source: An increase in pErk was also observed in 3D organotypic raft cultures treated with siRNA targeting COPS3 (Figure 3b).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3b

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of EGFR with AG1478 restores expression of differentiation markers Dsg1, Dsc1, and K10 in Cops3-deficient cultures.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of EGFR restored Dsg1, Dsc1, and K10 expression without increasing Cops3 protein levels (Figure 3c).
evidence: Western blot analysis of EGFR inhibitor treatment shown in Figure 3c

claim: The CSN, recruited to the desmosome through Cops3, is required to properly modulate EGFR activity.
source: These data are consistent with the hypothesis that the CSN, recruited to the desmosome through Cops3, is required to properly modulate EGFR activity.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from EGFR inhibitor rescue experiments

claim: EGFR neddylation occurs in NHEKs.
source: To address whether EGFR neddylation occurs in NHEKs and whether the desmosome-CSN complex regulates EGFR neddylation status, we performed RNAi-mediated silencing of DSG1, DP, and COPS3 in NHEKs differentiated for 1 day and assessed the association of the Nedd8 moiety with EGFR using PLA.
evidence: PLA assay detecting EGFR-Nedd8 association in NHEKs

claim: Silencing DP, DSG1, or COPS3 results in a significant increase in EGFR-Nedd8 PLA signals.
source: A significant increase in PLA positive signals between EGFR and Nedd8 was observed when DP, DSG1 or the CSN component COPS3 was silenced (Figure 4a and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), supporting a model whereby both the desmosome and the CSN are necessary for regulating EGFR de-neddylation.
evidence: PLA quantification shown in Figure 4a and Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: Loss of Dp or Cops3 via RNAi-mediated silencing results in elevated EGFR neddylation in SCC9 cells expressing HA-tagged Nedd8.
source: Loss of either Dp or Cops3 via RNAi-mediated silencing resulted in elevated EGFR neddylation (Figure 4b).
evidence: EGFR immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4b

claim: DP knockdown in desmosome-containing SCC9 cells impacts EGFR neddylation status, consistent with the observation that loss of either Dsg1 or Dp interferes with recruitment of Cops3 to desmosomes in NHEK cells.
source: The fact that DP knockdown in desmosome-containing SCC9 cells impacts EGFR neddylation status is consistent with the observation that loss of either Dsg1 or Dp interferes with recruitment of Cops3 to desmosomes in NHEK cells (Figure 1g and h).
evidence: Integration of data from Figure 4b with Figure 1g and h

claim: Loss of Cops3 and Dp results in reduced ubiquitination of EGFR in SCC9 cells treated with EGF.
source: Upon loss of Cops3 and Dp we observed reduced ubiquitination of EGFR (Figure 4c).
evidence: EGFR immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4c

claim: Silencing Dsg1, Cops3, or Dp results in a decrease in EGFR-Ubiquitin PLA signal.
source: We also found a decrease in a PLA signal between EGFR and Ubiquitin when Dsg1, Cops3, or Dp was silenced (Figure 4d).
evidence: PLA data shown in Figure 4d

claim: EGFR is ubiquitinated in Nedd8 depleted SCC9 cells, on average about 1.4-fold higher than control RNAi-treated cells.
source: Upon immunoprecipitation of EGFR, it was found that EGFR is ubiquitinated in Nedd8 depleted cells, on average about 1.4-fold higher than control RNAi-treated cells (Figure 4e).
evidence: EGFR immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4e

claim: PLA analysis reveals an association between EGFR and Ubiquitin upon the loss of Nedd8.
source: Additionally, PLA analysis revealed an association between EGFR and Ubiquitin upon the loss of Nedd8 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: PLA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: Both desmosome and CSN components support the generation and/or maintenance of ubiquitinated EGFR, at the expense of EGFR neddylation.
source: Overall, this suggests that both desmosome and CSN components support the generation and/or maintenance of ubiquitinated EGFR, at the expense of EGFR neddylation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from reciprocal relationship between neddylation and ubiquitination experiments

claim: EGFR border intensity remains elevated in cells silenced for COPS3, DSG1, and DP after treatment with EGF ligand for 5 minutes.
source: As shown in Figure 5a (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), EGFR border intensity in cells silenced for COPS3, DSG1, and DP remained elevated compared with control treated cultures after EGFR internalization was induced by treatment with EGF ligand.
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 5a and Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: EGFR intensity is dramatically reduced at cell-cell interfaces in both siCONT and siNEDD8 cultures at 15 minutes after EGF treatment, whereas EGFR is stable at borders in siCOPS3 cells.
source: EGFR intensity was dramatically reduced at cell-cell interfaces in both the siCONT and siNEDD8 cultures, whereas EGFR was stable at borders in siCOPS3 cells (Figure 5b and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 5b and Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: The desmosome-CSN complex destabilizes EGFR by de-neddylating the receptor.
source: These data are consistent with the idea that the desmosome-CSN complex destabilizes EGFR by de-neddylating the receptor.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from EGFR dynamics experiments

claim: Upon the loss of Nedd8, the stability of EGFR significantly decreases over a 24 hr time period in cycloheximide-treated NHEKs.
source: Our results indicate that upon the loss of Nedd8, the stability of EGFR significantly decreases over a 24 hr time period (Figure 5c).
evidence: Cycloheximide chase experiment shown in Figure 5c

claim: The neddylated state of EGFR promotes its stabilization.
source: These data are consistent with the idea that the neddylated state of EGFR promotes its stabilization.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from cycloheximide chase experiments

claim: EGFR is distributed more broadly throughout SCC9 and 1483 3D organotypic raft cultures and extends further into suprabasal layers than in control cultures or human epidermis.
source: In both cases, EGFR was distributed more broadly throughout the culture and extended further into suprabasal layers than in control cultures or human epidermis.
evidence: Observation from immunofluorescence of 3D raft cultures

claim: 1483 and SCC9 3D cultures exhibit elevated levels of EGFR and Cops3 compared to controls.
source: Additionally, 1483 and SCC9 3D cultures, when compared to controls, exhibited elevated levels of EGFR and Cops3 (Figure 6a).
evidence: Western blot analysis shown in Figure 6a

claim: The level of Dsg1, and to a lesser extent Dp, is reduced in the SCC9 and 1483 cancer 3D rafts when compared to control, primary NHEK 3D rafts.
source: However, the level of Dsg1, and to a lesser extent Dp, is reduced in the SCC9 and 1483 cancer 3D rafts when compared to control, primary NHEK 3D rafts (Figure 6a).
evidence: Western blot analysis shown in Figure 6a

claim: PLA analysis of organotypic cancer rafts reveals an increase in EGFR-Nedd8 signal.
source: PLA analysis of organotypic cancer rafts revealed an increase in EGFR-Nedd8, which is consistent with the known elevation of EGFR activity in HNSCC (Figure 6b top and middle panels).
evidence: PLA data shown in Figure 6b

claim: A reciprocal staining pattern of EGFR and Dsg1 is observed in organotypic cancer rafts.
source: Further, we observed a reciprocal staining pattern of EGFR and Dsg1 (Figure 6b bottom panel), consistent with the idea that loss of Dsg1 in progressing tumors is associated with elevated EGFR expression (Wong et al., 2008).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6b and cited literature

claim: Upon the loss of Cops3 in 3D raft cultures, there is an increase in Nedd8 associated with EGFR.
source: To show that proper CSN functioning is required for EGFR-neddylation maintenance in a 3D model, we carried out PLA analysis of rafts silenced for COPS3 and harvested at Day 3 (Figure 2c), and found that upon the loss of Cops3 there is an increase in Nedd8 associated with EGFR (Figure 6d).
evidence: PLA data shown in Figure 6d

claim: The desmosome scaffolds the CSN in proximity to EGFR to control the balance of neddylation-ubiquitination modifications, thus affecting receptor dynamics.
source: We propose a model by which the desmosome scaffolds the CSN in proximity to EGFR, to control the balance of neddylation-ubiquitination modifications, thus affecting receptor dynamics.
evidence: Model proposed based on integration of all experimental findings

claim: The CSN de-neddylation function contributes to EGFR turnover to promote differentiation in the epidermis.
source: Our data is consistent with a model whereby the CSN de-neddylation function contributes to EGFR turnover to promote differentiation in a regenerating tissue, in this case, the epidermis.
evidence: Model proposed based on integration of all experimental findings

claim: Loss of one CSN component affects the formation and function of the entire CSN.
source: Previous work has shown that the loss of one CSN component affects the formation and function of the entire CSN (Denti et al., 2006; Wei and Deng, 1999).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: Silencing of the COPS3 subunit is predicted to compromise the entire CSN.
source: Thus, silencing of the COPS3 subunit, shown here to interact with the desmosome, is predicted to compromise the entire CSN.
evidence: Inference based on cited literature about CSN function

claim: Silencing either DP or DSG1 disrupts the association of Cops3 with the other junction component.
source: Similarly, silencing either DP or DSG1 disrupts the association of Cops3 with the other junction component, consistent with the idea that entire desmosome is involved in scaffolding the CSN.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from PLA experiments with reciprocal knockdowns

claim: A mass spectrometry study identified multiple desmosomal proteins (Plakophilin2, Pg, Dsg1, and Dp), and not adherens junction proteins, as putative interactors with the first subunit (Cops1) of the COP9 signalosome.
source: This idea is further supported by a mass spectrometry study that identified multiple desmosomal proteins (Plakophilin2 (Pkp2), Pg, Dsg1, and Dp), and not adherens junction proteins, as putative interactors with the first subunit (Cops1) of the COP9 signalosome (Fang et al., 2012).
evidence: Cited from previous mass spectrometry study

claim: Desmosomal control over the neddylation-ubiquitination balance occurs in SCC9s and keratinocytes in the absence of Dsg1, supporting the idea that desmosomes of varying composition broadly regulate the CSN.
source: The fact that desmosomal control over the neddylation-ubiquitination balance occurs in SCC9s and keratinocytes in the absence of Dsg1 supports the idea that desmosomes of varying composition broadly regulate the CSN.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments in different cell types

claim: The majority of studies have linked neddylation with an increase in protein stability (e.g. MDM2, L11, HIF1α, and TβRII).
source: While one study reported a correlation between EGFR neddylation and degradation in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells, the majority of studies have linked neddylation with an increase in protein stability (e.g. MDM2 (Watson et al., 2010), L11 (Sundqvist et al., 2009), HIF1α (Ryu et al., 2011), and TβRII (Zuo et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from multiple previous studies

claim: Nedd8 and Ubiquitin compete for lysine residues on EGFR to regulate receptor dynamics.
source: Nevertheless, our data showing a reciprocal relationship between neddylated and ubiquitinated EGFR suggest that Nedd8 and Ubiquitin compete for lysine residues on EGFR to regulate receptor dynamics.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from reciprocal relationship experiments

claim: EGFR ubiquitination can occur independent of neddylation.
source: Furthermore, our data demonstrate that EGFR ubiquitination can occur independent of neddylation (Figure 4e and Figure 4—figure supplement 2), suggesting a new level of regulation that could have broad-reaching implications for receptor-mediated signaling in multiple contexts.
evidence: Data from Nedd8 knockdown experiments shown in Figure 4e and Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: EGFR has been shown to be a strong prognostic indicator in epithelial cancers, and increased expression has been associated with reduced survival rates in 70% of studies.
source: EGFR has been shown to be a strong prognostic indicator in epithelial cancers, and increased expression has been associated with reduced survival rates in 70% of studies (Nicholson et al., 2001).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: Elevation of EGFR in different types of cancer may be partly due to the stabilization of the receptor through increased neddylation.
source: This suggests the possibility that elevation of EGFR in different types of cancer may be partly due to the stabilization of the receptor through increased neddylation.
evidence: Speculation based on cancer model data and EGFR stability experiments

claim: Cops3 has been implicated in keratinocyte interleukin signaling.
source: Additionally, Cops3 has been implicated in keratinocyte interleukin signaling (Banda et al., 2005), which is interesting in light of the recent observation that loss of Dsg1 leads to an increase in inflammatory mediators in SAM syndrome, featuring severe dermatitis, multiple allergies, and metabolic wasting (Samuelov et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: Loss of Dsg1 leads to an increase in inflammatory mediators in SAM syndrome.
source: Additionally, Cops3 has been implicated in keratinocyte interleukin signaling (Banda et al., 2005), which is interesting in light of the recent observation that loss of Dsg1 leads to an increase in inflammatory mediators in SAM syndrome, featuring severe dermatitis, multiple allergies, and metabolic wasting (Samuelov et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: A desmosome-CSN super complex could serve as a general mechanism by which desmosomes regulate multiple downstream functions that guide normal skin homeostasis and paracrine signaling pathways in which keratinocytes participate.
source: A desmosome-CSN super complex could thus serve as a general mechanism by which desmosomes regulate multiple downstream functions that guide normal skin homeostasis and paracrine signaling pathways in which keratinocytes participate.
evidence: Speculation based on integration of findings with broader context

claim: Components of the desmosome-CSN super complex could provide new targets for treating diseases associated with inappropriate epidermal differentiation, inflammation, and cancer.
source: Further, components of this super complex could provide new targets for treating diseases associated with inappropriate epidermal differentiation, inflammation, and cancer.
evidence: Speculation about therapeutic implications

claim: Desmoglein 1 (Dsg1) is not only required for maintaining epidermal tissue integrity in superficial layers, but also promotes keratinocyte differentiation as cells transit out of the basal layer.
source: In particular, we showed that the desmosomal cadherin, Desmoglein 1 (Dsg1), is not only required for maintaining epidermal tissue integrity in superficial layers, but also promotes keratinocyte differentiation as cells transit out of the basal layer (Getsios et al., 2009).
evidence: Cited from previous work by the authors

claim: Dsg1 attenuates the activity of ErB receptors (EGFR and ErbB2) and downstream MAPK signaling.
source: It performs this function at least in part by attenuating the activity of ErB receptors (EGFR and ErbB2) and downstream MAPK signaling (Getsios et al., 2009; Harmon et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from previous work by the authors

claim: The unusually long cytoplasmic tail of Dsg1, but not the adhesive ectodomain, was required to suppress EGFR and Erk1/2 signaling.
source: The unusually long cytoplasmic tail of Dsg1, but not the adhesive ectodomain, was required to suppress EGFR and Extra Cellular Signal-regulated Kinase 1/2 (Erk1/2) signaling, indicating a previously unrecognized function for Dsg1 that transcends its canonical roles in adhesion.
evidence: Cited from previous work by the authors

claim: The CSN functions as a Nedd8 isopeptidase to remove Nedd8 moieties from its substrates, an activity depending on the Cops5 subunit.
source: The CSN functions as a Nedd8 isopeptidase to remove Nedd8 moieties from its substrates, an activity depending on the Cops5 subunit.
evidence: Established knowledge about CSN function

claim: The CSN de-neddylates cullin-RING E3 ligases (Cul1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b, 5, 7).
source: This hydrolysis has been classically studied in the context of de-neddylation of cullin-RING (Really Interesting New Gene) E3 ligases (Cul1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b, 5, 7) (Cope et al., 2002; Duda et al., 2008; Saha and Deshaies, 2008), which regulate fundamental processes important for development and tissue homeostasis, including cell cycle, signal transduction, transcription and DNA replication (Petroski and Deshaies, 2005).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: The CSN de-neddylates and partners with de-ubiquitinase enzymes to 'de-ubiquitinate' and rescue the cullin from spurious self-ubiquitination that occurs when the Nedd8 modification is present.
source: To promote the activity of cullin-RING E3 ligases, the CSN de-neddylates and partners with de-ubiquitinase enzymes to 'de-ubiquitinate' and rescue the cullin from spurious self-ubiquitination that occurs when the Nedd8 modification is present (Hetfeld et al., 2005; Wee et al., 2005; Zhou et al., 2003).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: Cells deficient for the CSN are unable to remove Nedd8, and as a consequence cullin-RING E3 ligase subunits are autoubiquitinated resulting in reduced function.
source: Cells deficient for the CSN are unable to remove Nedd8, and as a consequence cullin-RING E3 ligase subunits are autoubiquitinated resulting in reduced function (Bosu and Kipreos, 2008; Hetfeld et al., 2005; Hotton and Callis, 2008; Schwechheimer et al., 2001; Wee et al., 2005; Wu et al., 2005; Zhou et al., 2003).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: Ubiquitination is important for the internalization and post-internalization sorting of EGFR, where the ubiquitin ligase, Cbl, coordinates the transfer of the Ubiquitin from an E2 enzyme to the receptor's cytoplasmic domain.
source: Ubiquitination is important for the internalization and post-internalization sorting of EGFR, where the ubiquitin ligase, Cbl, coordinates the transfer of the Ubiquitin from an E2 enzyme to the receptor's cytoplasmic domain (Conte and Sigismund, 2016; Joazeiro et al., 1999; Levkowitz et al., 1999; Sorkin and Goh, 2008; Waterman et al., 1999; Yokouchi et al., 1999).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: When EGFR fails to acquire Ubiquitin, it is recycled back to the membrane.
source: When EGFR fails to acquire Ubiquitin, it is recycled back to the membrane (Levkowitz et al., 1998).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: Neddylation has previously been shown to stabilize substrates including other membrane receptors such as TGFβRII.
source: Further, neddylation has previously been shown to stabilize substrates including other membrane receptors such as TGFβRII (Zuo et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: Desmosomes are the most prominent cell-cell junctions in the epidermis.
source: In the epidermis, the most prominent of these junctions are desmosomes, which confer mechanical strength to tissues by linking the intermediate filament (IF) cytoskeleton through the IF anchoring protein Desmoplakin (Dp) to sites of desmosomal cadherin-mediated adhesion (Kowalczyk and Green, 2013).
evidence: Established knowledge about epidermal structure

claim: Desmosomes confer mechanical strength to tissues by linking the intermediate filament cytoskeleton through Desmoplakin to sites of desmosomal cadherin-mediated adhesion.
source: In the epidermis, the most prominent of these junctions are desmosomes, which confer mechanical strength to tissues by linking the intermediate filament (IF) cytoskeleton through the IF anchoring protein Desmoplakin (Dp) to sites of desmosomal cadherin-mediated adhesion (Kowalczyk and Green, 2013).
evidence: Established knowledge about desmosome function

claim: Mutations in genes encoding desmosome components lead to skin, heart, and hair defects.
source: The importance of the desmosome-IF complex is underscored by the existence of mutations in genes encoding desmosome components that lead to skin, heart, and hair defects (Lai-Cheong et al., 2007; Petrof et al., 2012).
evidence: Cited from previous literature

claim: The desmosome can act as a signaling scaffold to ensure the spatial and temporal execution of the epidermal differentiation program.
source: While the desmosome has classically been regarded as an adhesion complex, recent studies have demonstrated that it can act as a signaling scaffold to ensure the spatial and temporal execution of the epidermal differentiation program (Broussard et al., 2015; Harmon and Green, 2013; Schmidt and Koch, 2007; Sumigray and Lechler, 2015).
evidence: Cited from recent studies

claim: Dsg1 is first expressed as cells commit to differentiation and becomes progressively concentrated in the superficial epidermal layers.
source: Dsg1 is optimally positioned to exert this sort of spatial control on the EGFR pathway, as it is first expressed as cells commit to differentiation and becomes progressively concentrated in the superficial epidermal layers.
evidence: Established knowledge about Dsg1 expression pattern

claim: A yeast-two-hybrid screen using the cytoplasmic domain of Dsg1 as bait identified Cops3 as a putative binding partner.
source: To identify mediators of Dsg1 signaling functions we carried out a yeast-two-hybrid (Y2H) screen using the cytoplasmic domain of Dsg1 as bait (Harmon et al., 2013). Among the putative binding partners identified was the third subunit (Cops3) of the eight-subunit complex called the COP9 signalosome (CSN).
evidence: Yeast two-hybrid screen results

claim: The epidermis is a multi-layered epithelium that continuously renews itself through a highly choreographed program of morphological and biochemical changes.
source: The epidermis is a multi-layered epithelium that continuously renews itself through a highly choreographed program of morphological and biochemical changes, which are necessary to form a barrier against environmental insults and water loss (Koster and Roop, 2007).
evidence: Established knowledge about epidermal biology

claim: Epidermal renewal requires proliferating basal cells to stop dividing and undergo a commitment to differentiate as they transit toward the outer surface of the skin.
source: This process requires proliferating basal cells to stop dividing and undergo a commitment to differentiate as they transit toward the outer surface of the skin.
evidence: Established knowledge about epidermal differentiation

claim: Chemical cues governed by EGFR and other signaling receptors must be tightly regulated to maintain a proper balance of proliferation and differentiation in the epidermis.
source: Chemical cues governed by Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) and other signaling receptors must be tightly regulated to maintain a proper balance of proliferation and differentiation and to drive critical steps at each stage of epidermal stratification (Fuchs and Nowak, 2008; Fuchs and Raghavan, 2002; Koster and Roop, 2007; Lopez-Pajares et al., 2013).
evidence: Established knowledge about epidermal homeostasis

claim: Tissue morphogenesis and homeostasis are critically dependent on the proper spatial control of receptor tyrosine kinase activity.
source: Tissue morphogenesis and homeostasis are critically dependent on the proper spatial control of receptor tyrosine kinase activity (Casaletto and McClatchey, 2012).
evidence: Cited from previous literature
